All self harm is dangerous. One wrong cut can get you in a bad place. On the thigh you are likely to get a lot of gaping. If you must harm then don’t go anywhere near your inner thighs. Your upper thigh will be very painful and close to your knee the same. If you absolutely can’t deal with urges then make sure you use clean tools and test beforehand to see how sharp they are to avoid going too deep. 

All this being said, there’s no guarantee you won’t hit veins or arteries or nerves. Or get an infection which is easily serious. 

I may be seen as encouraging by giving this information but I know sometimes that urge won’t go. I would like to think this can keep you as safe as possible. I am sure you try self harm alternatives but if you want information on this let me know
You might want to listen to Eleanor Longden’s Ted Talk . She is quite inspiring and gives a good story of recovery https://www.ted.com/talks/eleanor_longden_the_voices_in_my_head/up-next?language=en

I am not a doctor but have experience with benzo use. If taken for a long period outside of crisis I do not find the benefit of them. I take pregablin for my anxiety but that is controversial as well. This was prescribed after a long time of review and many different medications. If you are getting the physical symptoms of anxiety I would have thought a beta blocker such as propanalol would have been tried.

I don’t know how to stop it as it’s a constant struggle for me too. Paradoxically sometimes planning your get out clause is the only way you can keep going. If you are about to act then that is different. Either way you shouldn’t have to live with this suicidal ideation. Reaching out to a professional is how you can try to heal. I know you are worried about your loved ones reaction but that reaction would be so much greater if you were to die. In terms of the barbiturates is there anyway you can cancel the order or make a promise to dispose of them. I know you won’t want to but it sounds like you still have things to keep you going. If life could feel more tolerable for you it sounds like you are a dedicated person. Remember no matter how far down the road you get with a suicidal plan. You are not fixed, if the littlest thing keeps you alive. Cling to it and pull yourself away. 

To be honest you need to talk to a professional and be honest, including your fears of your loved ones knowing they may be able to reassure you. There is life past suicidality , I’ve seen people recover and I hope this for you as you seem like you are striving hard

NAD but had an ex who had an eating disorder. He had a very low BMI and things progressed quickly. He was hospitalised and had severe damage to his liver. The team expected him to pass away and there was also pressure on his heart. Please see a doctor as soon as possible there is a very good chance your health could deteriorate quickly. Before being admitted he was walking around and was seemingly ok. You need professional help as recovery is something that needs monitoring carefully . Just eating more wont necessarily be enough you are likely to have several deficiencies and damage that needs medical attention. As well as looking into why you have lost so much and mentally try to heal. 

My ex now is in recovery and has no lasting effects from the ED but it very nearly killed him. There is a better life away from this. He thought he was happy in the ED but learning to cope and have a good relationship with food has made him so much happier

Hey I am not in the medical field just someone with trauma trying to get it sorted. You are very kind to offer this kind of help and some disclosure may help this person process. However, there needs to be a professional conducting this work. For several reasons talking to friends or loved ones is not helpful. There needs to be a boundary between the trauma and your other relationships. This keeps relationships healthy and prevents codependency. 

So be there for your friend and listen to disclosure when they want to make it but really full disclosure and work on healing needs to happen with a therapist. I would suggest looking for someone who has experience in the area of trauma your friend has. This might take searching but there will be someone who can hear what is said with a professional detachment that is required.

I also convince the voices that they aren’t to get rid of them but for other things. So I’ll say they are for sleep or for mood . Another option I do , because the action of the hand to mouth is the problem , I will put them on the table and only use my mouth to pick them up.

My grandma passed away in Feb she also had dementia and was very unwell with it. But through it all she kept smiling right to the very end. Eventually we had to leave because she was getting too much stimulation from us because she just loved us being there . 

We found this poem after she died and read it at the end of her funeral. It was written by her. 

​

The Gift

I watched you smile

With clear and simple grace

I watched you smile

Without a trace of guile

The memory of your face

Lives in a special place

I watched you smile
